Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the two Kiwi openers. Temba Bavuma and Co. are in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. It will be Will Young and Devon Conway to open the innings for New Zealand. Marco Jansen has the new ball in hand for South Africa. He has two slips in place. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, South Africa will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. Although the pitch is likely to get easier to bat under lights, it will not be that easy for New Zealand against the Proteas bowling unit which is even stronger with the return of Kagiso Rabada. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Quinton de Kock, one of the centurions for South Africa is down for a chat. He says he has been feeling really great lately and things are coming along for them and yes it is probably the best he has batted. Adds that New Zealand bowled really well up front, especially Trent Boult and he felt really scratchy and the guys just asked him through bat through and he managed to do well. Mentions that he is trying not to give it away and his career is coming to an end and wants to finish on a high. Reckons that the score on the board should be enough but the ball does come onto the bat better in the second but hopes that they can defend the score of 350 plus.

On the other hand, New Zealand started decently with the ball, but neither Tim Southee nor Matt Henry were able to pick an early wicket. The move to give Boult an extra over in his first spell paid off for Tom Latham and New Zealand as the left-arm seamer accounted for Temba Bavuma. In the middle phase, although the Kiwis were unable to pick up wickets, they did well not to leak boundaries and by doing so, did not allow South Africa to get away. At the halfway stage, it was even-stevens but a couple of overs later, Matt Henry pulled his hamstring and had to walk off, which meant that Tom Latham had to go looking around for bowling options. As a result, he had to give the ball to the likes of James Neesham and Glenn Phillips at the death and they were taken on by the Proteas batters. The Kiwis ended up conceding 119 runs in the last ten overs and they were unable to finish strongly with the ball.

THEY HAVE DONE IT AGAIN! Another 300-plus score by South Africa while batting first and this is their eighth consecutive 300-plus score in ODIs. After being inserted into bat by Tom Latham, it was a circumspect start from the two South African openers. It was Temba Bavuma who got himself going with a few boundaries early on, but he could not convert his start. Quinton de Kock started slower than some of his past innings, and he was happy to play himself in. Coming in at number 3, Rassie van der Dussen took his time and played the second fiddle throughout the 200-run stand. Seeing his partner struggle for timing, de Kock understood the need to kick on and soon notched up his fourth hundred of this World Cup. After the southpaw's departure, van der Dussen took up the mantle and shifted gears on his way to his century. Promoted up the order, David Miller did not get going straight away, but once he did, he unleashed himself all around the park. He registered his fifty off just 28 balls before Heinrich Klaasen's unbeaten 15 off 7 and Aiden Markram's last ball six took South Africa over 355.

SIX! BOOM! What a way to end the innings by Aiden Markram! Just one ball is what this in-form batter need and James Neesham is furious at himself. This is banged in short around off, Markram gets across his stumps, gets inside the line and pulls it with disdain over the fine leg fence for a biggie. 18 runs come off the final over and South Africa finish with 357/4 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-game rituals and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and the New Zealand players are taking their places on the field. Skipper, Temba Bavuma will open the innings for South Africa alongside Quinton de Kock as usual. Trent Boult has been handed the new ball and is raring to get going. A couple of slips in place, let's go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of this highly-anticipated contest but first, the two sets of players along with their mascots line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa first, followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

South Africa's captain Temba Bavuma says that they would have batted first anyway. Adds that batting first suits their makeup as a team. Shares that the wicket is on the drier side but feels that the ball will skid on under lights. Hopes that they can put up a good total and put New Zealand under pressure. Informs that Kagiso Rabada comes back in place of Tabraiz Shamsi. States that is important to continue with the momentum and they have taken a lot of confidence from the last game. Further adds that it was not a clinical win but the character shown was pleasing to see. Mentions that today is another opportunity to execute their skills and they will rely on the experience of guys who have played earlier against New Zealand in ODI World Cups. Adds that New Zealand have smart guys and they will have to make sure that they are switched on in all aspects of the game.

Tom Latham, the captain of New Zealand says that they will bowl first. Says that it looks like a reasonably good surface and dew might come on later. Informs that they have a few injury concerns and Tim Southee comes in for Lockie Ferguson. Mentions that they have been on the wrong side in the past couple of games but have got a good few days of practice and are ready for the contest. Ends by saying that South Africa isn't a team against whom they have played much ODI cricket in recent times but they did play them in the warm-up before the tournament.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Temba Bavuma (C), Rassie van der Dussen, Aiden Markram, Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Marco Jansen, Gerald Coetzee, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada (In for Tabraiz Shamsi), Lungi Ngidi.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Will Young, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (C/WK), Glenn Phillips, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Matt Henry, Tim Southee (In for Lockie Ferguson), Trent Boult.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of Tom Latham and New Zealand have opted to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Shaun Pollock is pitchside and he says that it is 33 degrees Celsius with a nice breeze blowing. Says that it is 62 meters and 67 meters on either side and low 70 meters straight. Adds that the breeze will come across the ground and make it easier to hit to the smaller side. Ricky Ponting joins him and says that it looks like a good wicket, nice and hard with some grass on it but it might be two-paced and will slow down later on. Mentions that in the last 6 D/N games, there has been an even split between teams batting first and second. Pollock ends by saying that there was seam movement in the evening.

After suffering a shock defeat against the Netherlands, the way South Africa have bounced back with three successive wins has proved that the loss was nothing but a minor blip. One of the major reasons for their success has been their batting unit's ability to rack up huge totals. Quinton de Kock has stood out, and he has found good support from Aiden Markram and Heinrich Klaasen. In the absence of Kagiso Rabada, who missed the game against Pakistan due to lower back spasms, Marco Jansen filled the void with an impressive showing while Tabraiz Shamsi justified his selection with a four-wicket haul. It has been more than two decades since South Africa last got the better of New Zealand in ODI World Cups. Will they manage to break the jinx? Or will New Zealand extend their dominance? Stay tuned as the toss and team news is coming up shortly.

The runners-up of the 2019 edition, New Zealand started their campaign with four wins in as many games. However, their campaign has hit a roadblock with two straight defeats, and they will be eager to return to winning ways. With Kane Williamson yet to fully recover, Daryl Mitchell and Rachin Ravindra will be expected to continue the good work with the bat. After scoring an unbeaten hundred against England, Devon Conway has seen a dip in form in recent games and he is due for a big score. In the last outing against Australia, Lockie Ferguson could not bowl much due to a right Achilles niggle, and the Kiwi fans will be hoping that the speedster is fit enough to feature. The pairing of Trent Boult and Matt Henry were put under pressure by the Aussie openers in the previous encounter and they would want to put in an improved display with the new ball.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of match number 32 of the 2023 ODI World Cup, which sees New Zealand take on South Africa. A blockbuster clash awaits us at Pune's Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium between two high-quality teams that currently occupy two of the top three spots in the standings, and we expect it to be a tightly fought contest.
